```{r libs, include = FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(mosaic)
library(testthat)
library(e1071)
```


```{r global-knitr-options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.pos = 'H',
                      fig.asp = 0.618,
                      fig.width = 4,
                      fig.cap = "",

                      cache = FALSE)
```






Question
========
Betrachten Sie die Histogramme. 


```{r solution, echo = FALSE}
sol_set <- c("MW < Md", "MW > Md", "Md < MW", "Md > MW")  

sol <- sample(sol_set, 1)
```


Wählen Sie das Histogramm, welches am deutlichsten folgende Eigenschaft  aufweist:


$`r sol`$



*Hinweis*: $MW$ steht für *Mittelwert* und $Md$ steht für *Median*.










```{r generate-data, echo = FALSE}
n <- 1000

d_symm <- rnorm(n = n) %>% zscore() %>%  as_tibble()
d_left1 <- rbeta(n, 5, 2) %>% zscore() %>% as_tibble()
d_right1 <- rbeta(n, 2, 5) %>% zscore() %>% as_tibble()

d_right2 <- rexp(n, 10) %>% zscore()%>% as_tibble()
d_left2 <- -rexp(n, 10) %>% zscore()%>% as_tibble()

d_uniform <- runif(n = n) %>% zscore() %>% as_tibble()




d_raw <- tibble(
  data = list(d_symm,
              d_uniform,
              #d_left1,
              d_left2,
              #d_right1,
              d_right2)) %>% 
    mutate(id = c("d_symm",
                  "d_uniform",
                  #"d_left1", 
                  "d_left2", 
                  #"d_right1", 
                  "d_right2"))



d <-
  d_raw %>% 
  mutate(skew = map_dbl(data, ~ e1071::skewness(.x[[1]]))) %>%  # as .x is a tibble, we need to access its first column
 # mutate(skew = unlist(skew)) %>% 
  mutate(avg = map_dbl(data, ~ mean(.x[[1]])),
         med = map_dbl(data, ~ median(.x[[1]])),
         med_minus_avg = med - avg) %>% 
  sample_n(size = nrow(.)) %>%   # shuffle it
  mutate(plot_id = LETTERS[1:nrow(.)])

```


```{r generate-solution, echo = FALSE}

d <- 
  d %>% 
  mutate(correct_plot = case_when(
    sol == "MW < Md" | sol == "Md > MW" ~ plot_id[which.min(skew)],
    sol == "MW > Md" | sol == "Md < MW"  ~ plot_id[which.max(skew)],
#    sol == "MW \\approx Md" ~ plot_id[which.min(abs(skew))],
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>% 
  mutate(is_correct = plot_id == correct_plot)

#stopifnot(d$is_correct[1] != NA)  # "`is_correct` must not be NA."
```




```{r generate-histograms, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, comment="", fig.width = 6, fig.asp = 0.7}

# all histograms in one figure, so that the PDF output stays within the page width
d_hist <- 
  d %>% 
  select(plot_id, data) %>% 
  unnest(data) %>% 
  mutate(plot_id = paste("Diagramm", plot_id))

ggplot(d_hist) +
  aes(x = value) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  facet_wrap(~ plot_id, scales = "free", ncol = 2)

```



```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
exams::answerlist(d$plot_id, markup = "markdown")
```




Solution
========

Das Histogramm ``r d$plot_id[d$is_correct == TRUE]`` zeigt die Eigenschaft $`r sol`$ am deutlichsten.


Aufgabenname: `schiefe-erkennen2`



```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
exams::answerlist(ifelse(d$is_correct, "Wahr", "Falsch"), markup = "markdown")
```
